objection:
I checked every part of P1 against the statement as written and found no error and no gap that can't be filled at once.

(i) Density. In (2)–(5), the congruences n≡l (mod q), m²|n can be solved exactly when (m²,q)|l. The solutions then form one class mod qm²/(m²,q). The counting error is ≤M, and the tail is ≤x/M. So the density exists and equals the stated series.

(ii) Local factors. The local factors in (7) are right for t=0, 1 and ≥2, including l=0. They give exactly the closed form (8) and the bound 0≤g≤1/q.

(iii) Second-moment identity. The local averages (12) and (13) check algebraically: 1+L(p), and (1−p⁻²)⁻¹ = 1+L(p)+L(p²). Splitting over prime powers by CRT then gives (14).

(iv) Bounds and sum. L(p)=A_p/p³ and L(p²)=A_p/p² with 0<A_p≤1, since the denominator minus the numerator is p²−p−1. This gives λ(ab²)≤c²a⁻³b⁻². The tail bound (19) holds for every T>0. Together they give Σ_{r>R}λ≤(10/3)R^{-1/2} and Σ_{r≤R}rλ≤(5/3)R^{1/2}. Since log(2R)>1 for R≥2, these imply the stated bounds with an absolute C. The Euler product gives Σλ=c²ζ(2)=c.

(v) Ramanujan series. |c_r(n)|≤φ(r) gives absolute convergence. The multiplicativity sketch in (24) is correct. Also c_p+c_{p²}=p²·1_{p²|n}−1, the local factors simplify to 1−2/p² and 1−1/p², and the ratio is (p²−1)/(p²−2). The series therefore equals 𝔖(n).

Numerical check (run locally): q·Σ_l g(q,l)² = Σ_{r|q}φ(r)G(r)²/… holds exactly, in exact rational arithmetic, for every q<60. The closed form for g matches brute-force counts of squarefree n≤10⁶ for several q and l. Σγ(r)²c_r(n) matches 𝔖(n) to about 7 digits for n=1, 4, 12, 36.

The proof cites no literature after 2010 and uses no dependencies.
